leg: Staging preview bar: URL-toggled JS injection, above nav, non-dismissable, manifest-backed last-updated (operator directive, ledger row 127)
operator_directive_verbatim: on the staging site ONLY, need the staging warning + last updated bar at top, above nav, non-dismissable. Maybe do it as a js injection feature toggled on the site url (match only root domain staging.protectsouthportland.*)
mechanism: ONE script (site/assets/js/staging-bar.js) shipped on every page in the same built bytes as production: at runtime it matches location.hostname against /^staging\.protectsouthportland\.[a-z]{2,}$/i (the root domain with any top-level domain variant, which also makes Chromium's *.localhost loopback mapping a real capture surface) and returns without rendering anything otherwise - production www/host variants, bare domains, localhost previews, file:// and attacker suffixes all render nothing. On match it injects the bar above .masthead (after the skip link).
timestamp_decision: the bar shows the SERVE manifest's fact: tools/staging_serve.py's prepare_serve_tree (with base_sha) writes staging-manifest.json into the SERVE tree - {served: UTC ISO at serve time, head: the fork sha the tree was built from} - and the bar fetches /staging-manifest.json and appends ' Last updated: <served> (serve <sha:12>)'. NO build-time fallback (deliberate, named): the built docs/ carry no volatile timestamp, so production and staging serve byte-identical trees and release freshness stays idempotent; when the manifest is unreachable the bar shows the warning without the updated line. The pin proves the timestamp lives in NO page's markup.
byte_comparison_note: served staging and production trees differ ONLY by the file the bar reads (staging-manifest.json, plus the serve tree's pre-existing robots/CNAME noindex injection), not by any page bytes
